docs.title: beesum-min
docs.text:
Transcript-first YouTube summarizer for the terminal. yt-dlp + WebVTT + local or API LLMs.

dotnet tool install -g beesum-min
beesum-min "https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=..." --timestamps

The default provider, transcript-only, never sends the transcript anywhere. ollama stays local. Cloud providers are opt-in.

docs.title: Start here
docs.text:
• Install — NuGet tool, Docker, source.
  • CLI — summarize, clip, save, JSON.
  • Library — embed the pipeline in .NET.
  • MCP — use it from Claude, Cursor, or another agent.
  • Editors — Vim, Emacs, pipes.
  • For agents — JSON, stdin, batch, exit codes.

docs.title: What it is not
docs.text:
• Not a hosted service; beesum-min is a local CLI/library.
  • Not a GUI; the GUI lives separately.
  • Not a promise that YouTube will never break — yt-dlp is maintained separately.

docs.title: Future server work
docs.text: The local core is intentionally host-agnostic. The planned ASP.NET service and chat connectors are documented under Server; they are not part of this repository.

docs.title: Adding an LLM provider
docs.text:
beesum-min talks to LLM backends through one small contract:

public interface ILlmProvider
{
    string Id { get; }
    string DisplayName { get; }

    Task<LlmAvailability> ProbeAsync(CancellationToken cancellationToken = default);

    Task<SummaryResult> SummarizeAsync(
        SummaryRequest request,
        CancellationToken cancellationToken = default);
}

The pipeline resolves exactly one provider by Id (CLI --provider <id>, or BeesumOptions.LlmProviderId) and calls SummarizeAsync. Everything else — prompt style, output format, transcript text — arrives inside SummaryRequest.

Built-in implementations (ollama, openai-compatible) are internal: register and select them through DI instead of constructing them directly. TranscriptOnlyLlmProvider is public because it is useful on its own.

docs.title: Walkthrough: a local HTTP backend
docs.text: The example below targets a fictional server that exposes POST /v1/complete and GET /health. Real implementations should follow the same shape.

docs.title: 1. Implement the provider
docs.text:
Create the provider in your own project (not inside Beesum.Core):

using System.Net.Http.Json;
using System.Text.Json;
using Beesum.Core.Abstractions;
using Beesum.Core.Llm;
using Beesum.Core.Models;

namespace MyApp;

public sealed class MyBackendLlmProvider : ILlmProvider
{
    private readonly IHttpClientFactory _httpClientFactory;
    private readonly string _baseUrl;
    private readonly string _model;

    public MyBackendLlmProvider(
        IHttpClientFactory httpClientFactory,
        string baseUrl,
        string model)
    {
        ArgumentNullException.ThrowIfNull(httpClientFactory);
        ArgumentException.ThrowIfNullOrWhiteSpace(baseUrl);
        ArgumentException.ThrowIfNullOrWhiteSpace(model);

        _httpClientFactory = httpClientFactory;
        _baseUrl = baseUrl.TrimEnd('/');
        _model = model;
    }

    public string Id => "my-backend";
    public string DisplayName => "My Backend";

    public async Task<LlmAvailability> ProbeAsync(CancellationToken cancellationToken = default)
    {
        using var cts = CancellationTokenSource.CreateLinkedTokenSource(cancellationToken);
        cts.CancelAfter(TimeSpan.FromSeconds(5));

        try
        {
            var client = _httpClientFactory.CreateClient("my-backend");
            using var response = await client.GetAsync($"{_baseUrl}/health", cts.Token);
            return response.IsSuccessStatusCode
                ? new LlmAvailability(true, ModelName: _model)
                : new LlmAvailability(false, $"HTTP {(int)response.StatusCode}");
        }
        catch (OperationCanceledException)
        {
            if (cancellationToken.IsCancellationRequested) throw;
            return new LlmAvailability(false, "Probe timed out.");
        }
        catch (Exception ex)
        {
            return new LlmAvailability(false, ex.Message);
        }
    }

    public async Task<SummaryResult> SummarizeAsync(
        SummaryRequest request,
        CancellationToken cancellationToken = default)
    {
        using var cts = CancellationTokenSource.CreateLinkedTokenSource(cancellationToken);
        cts.CancelAfter(TimeSpan.FromMinutes(2));

        try
        {
            var client = _httpClientFactory.CreateClient("my-backend");
            var payload = new
            {
                model = _model,
                prompt = LlmPrompts.BuildSystemPrompt(request)
                    + "\n\n" + request.Transcript.ToPlainText(),
            };

            using var response = await client.PostAsJsonAsync(
                $"{_baseUrl}/v1/complete", payload, cts.Token);

            if (!response.IsSuccessStatusCode)
            {
                var body = await response.Content.ReadAsStringAsync(cts.Token);
                return new SummaryResult(false, string.Empty, Id, $"HTTP {(int)response.StatusCode}: {body}");
            }

            using var doc = JsonDocument.Parse(
                await response.Content.ReadAsStringAsync(cts.Token));
            var content = doc.RootElement.GetProperty("text").GetString() ?? string.Empty;

            return new SummaryResult(
                true,
                content,
                Id,
                ModelName: doc.RootElement.TryGetProperty("model", out var m) ? m.GetString() : _model);
        }
        catch (OperationCanceledException)
        {
            if (cancellationToken.IsCancellationRequested) throw;
            return new SummaryResult(false, string.Empty, Id, "Summarize timed out.");
        }
        catch (Exception ex)
        {
            return new SummaryResult(false, string.Empty, Id, ex.Message);
        }
    }
}

Notes:

  • Register the HTTP client under a unique name; IHttpClientFactory clients are cheap and thread-safe.
  • ProbeAsync is informational today; the pipeline calls SummarizeAsync.
  • Return failures as SummaryResult(false, ..., error); do not throw for expected network errors. The pipeline and both hosts display ErrorMessage.
  • Fill ModelName, Usage (TokenUsage), and Duration when your backend reports them — CLI --json exposes these fields.
  • Respect SummaryRequest.Instructions and SummaryRequest.SystemPrompt. LlmPrompts.BuildSystemPrompt(request) already does that.
  • Never log API keys or transcript content.

LlmPrompts.BuildSystemPrompt(request) is public, so your provider does not have to reimplement style, format, or instruction handling.

docs.title: 2. Register it in DI
docs.text:
services.AddBeesum(options =>
{
    options.LlmProviderId = "my-backend";
    options.OllamaBaseUrl = null; // only if you do not want the local provider
});

services.AddHttpClient("my-backend");
services.AddSingleton<ILlmProvider>(sp =>
    new MyBackendLlmProvider(
        sp.GetRequiredService<IHttpClientFactory>(),
        "http://localhost:8080",
        "my-model"));

The pipeline factory enumerates ILlmProvider registrations when it is resolved, so the order of AddBeesum and your registration does not matter. The provider list is visible to hosts through DI; a UI can build its dropdown from IEnumerable<ILlmProvider> without changes.

To switch providers at run time (instead of configuring one in BeesumOptions), use ISummarizerPipelineFactory:

var pipeline = factory.Create("my-backend");

docs.title: 3. Test it
docs.text:
Use Beesum.Testing (InMemoryHttpMessageHandler, InMemoryHttpClientFactory, InMemoryLlmProvider) or plain fakes; no mocking library is required:

using Beesum.Testing;

var handler = new InMemoryHttpMessageHandler()
    .EnqueueJson("""{"text":"summary"}""");
var provider = new MyBackendLlmProvider(
    new InMemoryHttpClientFactory(handler), "http://localhost:9999", "m");

var result = await provider.SummarizeAsync(
    new SummaryRequest(transcript, PromptStyle.Neutral, OutputFormat.PlainText));

Assert.True(result.IsSuccess);
Assert.Equal("summary", result.Content);
Assert.Equal("my-backend", result.ProviderId);

Cover at least: success, non-2xx response, malformed JSON, timeout, and ProbeAsync.

docs.title: 4. Verify manually
docs.text:
dotnet run --project src\Beesum.Min.Cli -- --local-vtt samples/demo/smoke.vtt --provider my-backend

Because the provider list is resolved through DI, forgetting step 2 produces LLM provider 'my-backend' is not registered.

docs.title: Checklist
docs.text:
• [ ] Id is stable, lowercase, and unique.
  • [ ] All HTTP calls have timeouts and honor the cancellation token.
  • [ ] Expected failures return SummaryResult(false, ...); exceptions are reserved for bugs.
  • [ ] Metadata (ModelName, Usage, Duration) is filled when available.
  • [ ] No secrets or transcript text in logs or exception messages.
  • [ ] Registered in DI and reachable from the CLI (--provider).
  • [ ] Tests cover success, HTTP error, bad JSON, and timeout.
  • [ ] dotnet build and the test projects are clean.

docs.title: API providers
docs.text:
beesum-min can summarize with a local model or a cloud API. Cloud keys are read from environment variables only — passing a key as an argument puts it in your shell history and in the process list.

--provider API Key variable Default endpoint openai OpenAI-compatible OPENAI_API_KEY https://api.openai.com anthropic (alias claude) Anthropic Messages ANTHROPIC_API_KEY https://api.anthropic.com gemini (alias google) Google Gemini GEMINI_API_KEY or GOOGLE_API_KEY https://generativelanguage.googleapis.com

The OpenAI-compatible provider is the lowest common denominator: it works with OpenAI, OpenRouter, Groq, Together, LM Studio, llama.cpp server, and anything else that speaks /v1/chat/completions.

docs.title: Examples
docs.text:
# OpenAI
$env:OPENAI_API_KEY = "sk-..."
beesum-min "https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=..." --provider openai

# OpenRouter
$env:OPENROUTER_API_KEY = "sk-or-..."
beesum-min "https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=..." --provider openai `
  --api-url https://openrouter.ai/api `
  --api-model anthropic/claude-sonnet-4-5 `
  --api-key-env OPENROUTER_API_KEY

# Groq
$env:GROQ_API_KEY = "gsk_..."
beesum-min "..." --provider openai `
  --api-url https://api.groq.com/openai `
  --api-model llama-3.3-70b-versatile `
  --api-key-env GROQ_API_KEY

# Local LM Studio (no key needed)
beesum-min "..." --provider openai `
  --api-url http://localhost:1234 `
  --api-model qwen2.5-7b-instruct

# Anthropic
$env:ANTHROPIC_API_KEY = "sk-ant-..."
beesum-min "..." --provider anthropic
beesum-min "..." --provider anthropic --api-model claude-sonnet-4-5 --max-tokens 2048

# Gemini
$env:GEMINI_API_KEY = "..."
beesum-min "..." --provider gemini
beesum-min "..." --provider gemini --api-model gemini-2.5-flash

--api-url, --api-model, and --api-key-env apply to the selected API provider and ignore the defaults above. --max-tokens is used by Anthropic and Gemini (Anthropic requires it; Gemini uses it as maxOutputTokens).

docs.title: Retries and timeouts
docs.text:
• Requests are attempted up to three times on HTTP 429 and 5xx.
  • Retry-After is honored, capped at five seconds.
  • A request has a two-minute timeout; cancellation is passed through.

docs.title: Errors
docs.text:
Situation What you get Key variable is not set No API key for <provider>. Set ... and exit code 2 Key is rejected invalid API key in the result / JSON Rate limit survives retries rate limited; retry later Model name is wrong the provider's HTTP error, truncated to 300 chars Prompt blocked (Gemini) Prompt blocked: <reason>

With --json, the same text is in errorMessage; exit code 1.

docs.title: From the library
docs.text:
services.AddBeesum(options =>
{
    options.LlmProviderId = "anthropic";
    options.AnthropicBaseUrl = "https://api.anthropic.com";
    options.AnthropicModel = "claude-sonnet-4-5";
    options.AnthropicApiKeyProvider = _ =>
        Task.FromResult(Environment.GetEnvironmentVariable("ANTHROPIC_API_KEY"));
    options.MaxOutputTokens = 2048;
});

GeminiBaseUrl/GeminiModel/GeminiApiKeyProvider work the same way. The built-in providers are internal: configure them through BeesumOptions instead of constructing them.

docs.title: Notes
docs.text:
• Model names and prices change. The defaults are a starting point, not a promise.
  • API providers see the transcript. transcript-only and ollama do not leave your machine.
  • A 200 response with an empty body is treated as a failure, not as an empty summary.

docs.title: Chunking long transcripts
docs.text: Providers have input limits. Instead of failing on a two-hour podcast, the pipeline splits the transcript, summarizes each part, and combines the parts.

docs.title: When it happens
docs.text:
Chunking is on by default. It triggers when the estimated transcript size exceeds ChunkTokens (default 6000). The estimate is deliberately rough: characters divided by three, not a real tokenizer. Latin text is over-estimated, Cyrillic and CJK are closer to the truth. Over-estimating means one extra chunk, which is cheaper than a context overflow.

CLI controls:

beesum-min "..." --chunk-tokens 4000
beesum-min "..." --no-chunk

Library controls:

services.AddBeesum(options =>
{
    options.ChunkLongTranscripts = true;
    options.ChunkTokens = 4000;
});

docs.title: How it works
docs.text:
1. Map. The transcript is cut on segment boundaries; an oversized segment is cut on word boundaries. Each chunk gets a fixed instruction: summarize this part, keep names, numbers, decisions, and conclusions.
  2. Reduce. The partial summaries are combined with the original style, format, and instructions. If the partials themselves exceed ChunkTokens, they are grouped and reduced again, up to three levels.
  3. Result. SummaryResult contains the final text, the summed Usage, the total Duration, and the model reported by the final call.

Progress reports Chunking once, then Completed when the final summary is ready. A failed chunk fails the whole run with Chunk <i>/<n> failed: ...; the pipeline does not silently combine incomplete input.

docs.title: Cost and privacy
docs.text:
Every chunk is a provider call. With a cloud API that means more tokens and more money; --json shows the total in usage so you can measure it. With transcript-only and ollama nothing leaves the machine, but chunks still mean extra calls.

A full SystemPrompt override applies to both map and reduce calls, so a custom prompt must make sense for a partial summary as well as for the final answer. Instructions apply to the final combination; map calls use the fixed part-summary instruction.

docs.title: Limitations
docs.text:
• The estimate is not a tokenizer; very unusual languages can be under-counted.
  • Timestamps are not preserved in summaries; chunks carry the original segment times only as metadata.
  • A single chunk larger than the model context is still possible if the provider rejects it; there is no automatic retry with a smaller chunk.

docs.title: CLI
docs.text:
# Transcript only
beesum-min "https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=..." 

# Local Ollama
beesum-min "..." --provider ollama --ollama-model qwen3:1.7b --format markdown

# JSON for scripts
beesum-min "..." --json

# Clip and save
beesum-min "..." --from 00:12:34 --to 00:18:00 --timestamps `
  --save-vtt clip.vtt --save-transcript clip.md -o notes.md

# stdin
Get-Content captions.vtt | beesum-min --stdin --input vtt --timestamps

# Batch
beesum-min --batch urls.txt --jsonl

docs.title: Flags
docs.text:
Flag Meaning --provider transcript-only, ollama, openai, anthropic, gemini --style historian, programmer, neutral --format markdown, plaintext, mindmap --prompt-file full system-prompt override --instructions append to the built-in prompt --timestamps [hh:mm:ss] cues and timestamp-aware prompts --from / --to clip transcript by time --save-vtt copy the full VTT --save-transcript write the clipped transcript/summary --json one stable object --jsonl one object per batch item --stdin read a transcript from stdin --batch one URL per line --no-chunk disable map-reduce chunking --proxy passed to yt-dlp

Progress goes to stderr; stdout is the result (or JSON).

docs.title: Doctor
docs.text:
beesum-min doctor
beesum-min doctor --json
beesum-min doctor --check-updates

Checks yt-dlp, deno, temp, Ollama, and the selected provider's key. Update checks are opt-in and never download anything.

docs.title: Editors and pipes
docs.text: beesum-min reads a transcript from stdin, so you do not need a plugin to use it from an editor. Progress goes to stderr; stdout is the summary (or JSON).

docs.title: Shell pipes
docs.text:
# Already downloaded subtitles
Get-Content .\captions.vtt | beesum-min --stdin --input vtt

# Any plain text: a transcript, an article, a meeting note
Get-Content .\transcript.txt | beesum-min --stdin --input text --format markdown

# JSON for scripts and editor plugins
Get-Content .\transcript.txt | beesum-min --stdin --json

--input defaults to text, so --stdin alone is enough for plain text.

docs.title: Clips and saves
docs.text:
Clip by transcript time and keep both files:

beesum-min "https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=..." `
  --from 00:12:34 --to 00:18:00 --timestamps `
  --save-vtt clip.vtt --save-transcript clip.md `
  -o notes.md --no-save-prompt
  • --from / --to accept ss, mm:ss, or hh:mm:ss and slice the transcript, not the video. The raw VTT stays complete.
  • --save-vtt keeps the downloaded/local VTT; --save-transcript writes the clipped text or summary; -o writes the notes/summary file.
  • Without the save flags, an interactive terminal asks once per file: Save transcript? [y/N] and Save subtitles (VTT)? [y/N], then the path. --no-save-prompt disables the questions. Piped, JSON, batch, and stdin runs never prompt, so scripts cannot hang.

Paths are explicit; nothing is written into a hidden library automatically. Create a folder and pass a path when you want one:

--save-transcript notes\caching.md --save-vtt notes\caching.vtt

From Vim/Neovim, insert a clip below the cursor without replacing the buffer:

:r !beesum-min "https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=..." --from 00:12:34 --to 00:18:00 --timestamps --no-save-prompt

docs.title: Vim / Neovim
docs.text:
No plugin is required; the built-in filter is enough:

" Replace the current buffer with a summary (undo with u)
:%!beesum-min --stdin --input text

" Replace the selected lines
:'<,'>!beesum-min --stdin --input text

For a scratch buffer instead of replacing text, load contrib/vim/beesum.vim (copy it to ~/.vim/plugin/, or use a plugin manager) and:

:BeesumUrl https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=...
:'<,'>BeesumSelection
:BeesumBuffer

If the binary is not beesum-min, set g:beesum_min_command. Extra flags go to g:beesum_min_arguments.

Neovim:

vim.opt.runtimepath:append("/path/to/beesum-min/contrib/vim")

docs.title: Emacs
docs.text:
Load contrib/emacs/beesum.el:

(load-file "/path/to/beesum-min/contrib/emacs/beesum.el")
(global-set-key (kbd "C-c b u") #'beesum-min-url)
(global-set-key (kbd "C-c b r") #'beesum-min-region)

M-x beesum-min-url prompts for a URL; M-x beesum-min-region summarizes the active region. Results open in *beesum-min* in special-mode.

docs.title: Notes
docs.text:
• --json is the stable interface for plugins; parse content and ignore progress on stderr.
  • On Windows, a global tool lives in %USERPROFILE%\.dotnet\tools; make sure that directory is in PATH, or set g:beesum_min_command to the full path.
  • Editors usually add a trailing newline; it ends up in the transcript. Harmless.

docs.title: Embedding Beesum.Core
docs.text:
This guide shows how to use the Core library from your own application: register the services, run the pipeline, read the result metadata, plug in a custom LLM provider, and test everything without network access.

The package targets .NET 10 and follows 0.x versioning: the public API may still change between minor releases.

docs.title: 1. Install
docs.text:
dotnet add package Beesum.Core
dotnet add package Beesum.Testing   # in test projects

docs.title: 2. Register the services
docs.text:
using Beesum.Core.Abstractions;
using Beesum.Core.DependencyInjection;
using Beesum.Core.Models;
using Microsoft.Extensions.DependencyInjection;

var services = new ServiceCollection();

services.AddBeesum(options =>
{
    options.LlmProviderId = "transcript-only"; // or "ollama"
    options.OllamaBaseUrl = "http://localhost:11434"; // set to null to skip Ollama
    options.OllamaModel = "llama3.2";
});

await using var provider = services.BuildServiceProvider();
var pipeline = provider.GetRequiredService<ISummarizerPipeline>();

AddBeesum registers contracts and their default implementations and exposes the same values as IOptions<BeesumOptions>:

var options = provider.GetRequiredService<IOptions<BeesumOptions>>().Value;

The container structure (which providers exist, where yt-dlp comes from) is decided at registration time. Mutating the options object afterwards does not re-register services.

docs.title: Options
docs.text: Property Default Purpose YtDlpPath null Explicit yt-dlp path; null auto-detects settings → tools/ → PATH. OllamaBaseUrl http://localhost:11434 Ollama URL; null/empty disables the provider. OllamaModel llama3.2 Ollama model name. OpenAiBaseUrl null OpenAI-compatible URL; null/empty disables the provider. OpenAiModel gpt-4o-mini OpenAI-compatible model name. OpenAiApiKeyProvider null API-key callback; null reads openai.apiKey from ISecretStore. LlmProviderId transcript-only Provider used by the default pipeline. SubtitlesDirectory null Persistent subtitle directory; null uses a temp directory. StorageRoot platform default Root for settings, secrets, cache, and history. YtDlpExtraArgs empty Extra arguments for every yt-dlp call (--proxy, cookies, ...). SubtitleLanguages en yt-dlp --sub-langs selectors, in preference order. ChunkLongTranscripts true Split transcripts over ChunkTokens and combine partial summaries. ChunkTokens 6000 Approximate input budget per chunk.

docs.title: From a local subtitle file
docs.text:
var result = await pipeline.RunAsync(
    new SummarizeCommand(
        Url: string.Empty,
        PromptStyle.Neutral,
        OutputFormat.Markdown,
        LocalVttPath: "captions.vtt"),
    progress: null,
    cancellationToken: CancellationToken.None);

if (!result.IsSuccess)
{
    Console.Error.WriteLine(result.ErrorMessage);
    return;
}

Console.WriteLine(result.Content);

docs.title: From a YouTube URL
docs.text:
var result = await pipeline.RunAsync(
    new SummarizeCommand(
        Url: "https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=...",
        PromptStyle.Historian,
        OutputFormat.Markdown),
    cancellationToken: cancellationToken);

The URL path needs yt-dlp to be installed (or pointed to by YtDlpPath). The library never starts a download on its own: a call to RunAsync is the user action.

docs.title: Progress
docs.text:
Stages are reported in order: Starting, Downloading, Parsing, Summarizing, Completed. Completed fires only on success.

var progress = new Progress<PipelineStage>(stage => Console.WriteLine(stage));
await pipeline.RunAsync(command, progress);

IProgress<T> callbacks may run on the captured synchronization context; pass a synchronous implementation in tests if order matters.

docs.title: 4. Read the result
docs.text:
SummaryResult is a record:

Member Meaning IsSuccess Whether a summary was produced. Content Summary text, or empty on failure. ProviderId Provider that produced the result; null if the pipeline failed early. ErrorMessage Human-readable failure reason on failure. ModelName Model reported by the provider, when known. Usage TokenUsage (prompt/completion/total), when the backend reports it. Duration Time spent in the provider call.

Expected failures (missing subtitles, HTTP errors, timeouts) come back as IsSuccess == false; exceptions are reserved for programming errors and cancellation.

docs.title: 5. Choose a provider at run time
docs.text:
ISummarizerPipelineFactory creates a pipeline for a provider id:

var factory = provider.GetRequiredService<ISummarizerPipelineFactory>();
var ollama = factory.Create("ollama");

Use it when the provider is selected dynamically (a UI dropdown, a batch job with mixed settings). Unknown ids fail inside RunAsync with a descriptive error.

docs.title: 6. Custom prompts
docs.text:
SummaryRequest accepts two optional fields:

new SummaryRequest(
    transcript,
    PromptStyle.Neutral,
    OutputFormat.Markdown,
    Instructions: "Five bullets, no fluff.",
    SystemPrompt: null); // set to replace the built prompt entirely

Instructions is appended to the style/format prompt. SystemPrompt, when set, wins and the style/format text is ignored. The same fields exist on SummarizeCommand, which is what the CLI uses.

LlmPrompts.BuildSystemPrompt(request) applies the rules; custom providers should call it instead of rebuilding the prompt.

docs.title: 7. Custom providers
docs.text:
Implement ILlmProvider, register it after AddBeesum, and point LlmProviderId/Create at its Id. Reuse the public prompt builder LlmPrompts.BuildSystemPrompt(style, format). See adding-a-provider.md for a full walkthrough.

Built-in implementations are internal; register and select them through DI.

docs.title: 8. Logging
docs.text:
Core services accept ILogger<T> and default to NullLogger. Register logging before building the provider:

services.AddLogging(builder => builder.AddConsole());

No transcript content, API keys, or cookies are logged.

docs.title: 9. Testing
docs.text:
var services = new ServiceCollection();
services.AddBeesum(options => options.OllamaBaseUrl = null);
services.AddBeesumTesting();

await using var provider = services.BuildServiceProvider();

AddBeesumTesting() replaces storage, yt-dlp, parser, process runner, and providers with in-memory doubles. Override a single double afterwards by registering it last:

services.AddSingleton<ILlmProvider>(new InMemoryLlmProvider("ollama"));

InMemoryProcessRunner records every invocation, so you can assert the exact argument list (the library always uses ProcessStartInfo.ArgumentList).

docs.title: 10. Storage
docs.text:
The default root is %APPDATA%\Beesum on Windows and ~/.config/Beesum elsewhere. It contains settings.json, secrets.dat, transcripts/, and history.jsonl. At the moment the pipeline consumes only the ytdlp.path setting; the cache and history contracts exist for hosts to use.

DpapiSecretStore uses DPAPI on Windows; on other platforms it stores secrets in plain files in the same directory, so keep that path private.

docs.title: 11. Lifetime and threading
docs.text: All registered services are singletons and stateless per request: a single pipeline can process independent commands concurrently. SummaryResult is immutable; pass CancellationToken to stop work promptly.

docs.title: For LLM agents and scripts
docs.text: The CLI is built to be called by a program, not only by a person. Everything it prints is either the summary or a line of progress on stderr.

docs.title: Contract
docs.text:
• --json prints one object; --jsonl prints one compact object per batch item.
  • Exit codes: 0 success, 1 runtime failure, 2 invalid arguments.
  • Progress goes to stderr; stdout stays parseable.
  • --stdin --input text|vtt accepts a transcript from another tool.
  • --batch <file> takes one URL per line, skips blanks and # comments.
  • --prompt-file replaces the system prompt; --instructions appends to it.
  • API keys are read from environment variables, never from arguments.

The JSON shape is documented in json-output.md, including the batch object with its url field.

docs.title: Recipes
docs.text:
# Get only the text
beesum-min "https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=..." --json | jq -r '.content'

# Fail the script when the summary failed
beesum-min "..." --json | jq -e '.isSuccess' >/dev/null

# Summarize a transcript produced by another tool
cat transcript.vtt | beesum-min --stdin --input vtt --json > out.json

# Batch, with per-item URLs in the output
beesum-min --batch urls.txt --jsonl > results.jsonl

docs.title: What an agent should not do
docs.text:
• Do not re-summarize the returned content with another model; you already have the summary.
  • Do not paste the transcript into --prompt-file; it is sent separately as the user message and will be duplicated.
  • Do not pass API keys on the command line; they end up in shell history and process listings. Use the provider's environment variable.
  • Do not ignore isSuccess; content is an empty string on failure.

docs.title: Why this is agent-friendly
docs.text:
• No telemetry, no call-home, no background network activity.
  • transcript-only needs no model and no network beyond yt-dlp.
  • Chunking keeps long transcripts inside the model's context.
  • usage in JSON is the sum of every provider call, so cost is measurable.
  • The test suite is offline and deterministic; CI runs on Windows and Linux.

For a native agent interface use beesum-mcp: it exposes the same pipeline as summarize_url and summarize_transcript over MCP. The JSON/stdin contract above remains the stable fallback for scripts.

docs.title: Good first issues
docs.text:
Scoped starter tasks. Copy one into a GitHub issue (or pick it up directly), keep the change buildable with tests, and open an issue first for anything large.

Each item lists the goal, the files that are usually involved, and a definition of done. Sizes are rough: S is an afternoon, M is a day or two.

docs.title: 1. Wire ITranscriptCache into the pipeline (M)
docs.text:
Goal. Avoid re-downloading subtitles for the same video.

Where. src/Beesum.Core/Pipeline/SummarizerPipeline.cs, src/Beesum.Core/Storage/FileTranscriptCache.cs, src/Beesum.Core/DependencyInjection/ServiceCollectionExtensions.cs.

Done when. A cached transcript is used when present and fresh, a cache hit is observable in the result/progress, cache writes are atomic, and tests cover hit, miss, stale entry, and corruption.

docs.title: 2. Persist summary history (M)
docs.text:
Goal. Make ISummaryHistory real instead of an unused contract.

Where. src/Beesum.Core/Pipeline/SummarizerPipeline.cs, src/Beesum.Core/Storage/JsonSummaryHistory.cs.

Done when. Every successful run appends an entry (id, source id, title, provider, style, timestamp), the JSONL format has a documented schema, and tests cover append, read, remove, and corrupt lines.

docs.title: 3. First-run yt-dlp setup (M)
docs.text:
Goal. Remove the "install yt-dlp yourself" step for CLI users.

Where. src/Beesum.Core/YtDlp/YtDlpPathResolver.cs, src/Beesum.Core/YtDlp/YtDlpService.cs, CLI flags.

Done when. A new beesum-min --install-yt-dlp command downloads the binary into tools/ with progress and checksum/size sanity checks, never runs without the explicit flag, and has tests for the happy path and HTTP failure.

docs.title: 4. Actionable yt-dlp error messages (S)
docs.text:
Goal. Turn raw yt-dlp stderr into guidance.

Where. src/Beesum.Core/YtDlp/YtDlpService.cs, src/Beesum.Core/Models/SubtitleDownloadResult.cs.

Done when. 429, 403, "Sign in to confirm you're not a bot", DNS failure, and timeouts map to short messages with the suggested next step (sleep, cookies, proxy, JS runtime), covered by tests with representative stderr samples.

docs.title: 5. Golden-file tests for real-world WebVTT variants (S)
docs.text:
Goal. Harden the parser against formats not covered by hand-written fixtures.

Where. tests/Beesum.Core.Tests/Parsing/, new fixtures/*.vtt.

Done when. At least five sanitized real-world files (YouTube auto-captions, manual captions, styled cues, multi-line cues, non-English) are parsed and compared against reviewed expected text; the fixtures contain no personal data.

docs.title: 6. Make the CLI trim- and AOT-friendly (M)
docs.text:
Goal. -p:PublishTrimmed=true currently breaks the LLM providers because PostAsJsonAsync uses reflection-based System.Text.Json.

Where. src/Beesum.Core/Llm/OllamaLlmProvider.cs, OpenAiCompatibleLlmProvider.cs, src/Beesum.Min.Cli/Beesum.Min.Cli.csproj.

Done when. Request/response payloads use a source-generated JsonSerializerContext, a trimmed publish runs the local-vtt and Ollama smoke tests, and the measured size is documented.

docs.title: 7. --yt-dlp-args-file and escape support (S)
docs.text:
Goal. Make complex yt-dlp invocations maintainable.

Where. src/Beesum.Min.Cli/CliOptionsParser.cs, HelpText.cs, tests/Beesum.Min.Cli.Tests/.

Done when. --yt-dlp-args-file <path> reads arguments from a file (one argument per line, # comments), backslash escapes such as \" work in --yt-dlp-args, and tests cover quoting, escapes, comments, and invalid files.

docs.title: 8. Batch mode (M)
docs.text:
Goal. Summarize a list of URLs in one invocation.

Where. src/Beesum.Min.Cli/, src/Beesum.Core/Pipeline/.

Done when. --batch <file> accepts one URL per line, reports per-item success and failure, supports --json as JSON Lines or an array, keeps a single provider instance, and is covered by tests.

docs.title: 9. Docker image smoke test in CI (S)
docs.text:
Goal. Turn the local Dockerfile into a tested artifact.

Where. .github/workflows/ci.yml, Dockerfile.

Done when. CI builds the Linux image, runs docker run --rm beesum-min --help and a local .vtt smoke test, and the README shows the real image size.

docs.title: 10. JSON contract test (S)
docs.text:
Goal. Lock the --json shape so scripts do not break silently.

Where. tests/Beesum.Min.Cli.Tests/JsonOutputTests.cs, new fixtures/json/*.json.

Done when. Serialized output is compared against reviewed golden files for success, failure, and metadata-present cases, and the expected field set is asserted explicitly.

docs.title: Canonical source
docs.text:
• GitHub: https://github.com/air-catfish/beesum-min
  • Codeberg mirror: https://codeberg.org/air-catfish/beesum-min

docs.title: Documentation site
docs.text:
The site is a static MkDocs Material build published from the gh-pages branch:

https://air-catfish.github.io/beesum-min/

GitHub Pages is configured once with Settings → Pages → Deploy from a branch → gh-pages / root. The branch contains only generated HTML and assets; it does not add commits to main.

Build locally:

python -m mkdocs build --clean

The Suprematist theme lives in docs/assets/stylesheets/suprematism.css. The repository also ships assets/readme-banner.png and assets/social-preview.png for GitHub/Codeberg presentation.

docs.title: Codeberg mirror

docs.title: Migration
docs.text: The site is static. If GitHub Pages is unavailable, copy the generated directory to any static host and change site_url in mkdocs.yml.

docs.title: .NET tool
docs.text:
Requires the .NET 10 runtime.

dotnet tool install -g beesum-min
dotnet tool install -g beesum-mcp

docs.title: Library
docs.text:
dotnet add package Beesum.Core
dotnet add package Beesum.Testing   # test projects

docs.title: Docker
docs.text:
docker run --rm -v "$PWD:/out" ghcr.io/air-catfish/beesum-min:latest \
  "https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=..." -o /out/summary.md

The image includes yt-dlp and deno.

docs.title: From source
docs.text:
dotnet build beesum-min.slnx -c Release
dotnet run --project src\Beesum.Min.Cli -- --local-vtt samples\demo\talk.vtt

yt-dlp must be in PATH, in tools/ next to the executable, or passed with --yt-dlp.

docs.title: Check the environment
docs.text:
beesum-min doctor
beesum-min doctor --check-updates

docs.title: JSON output
docs.text: beesum-min --json writes one JSON object to stdout (or to the file passed with -o/--output) instead of human-readable text. Progress messages go to stderr, so stdout stays valid JSON.

docs.title: Invocation
docs.text:
beesum-min --local-vtt .\captions.vtt --json
beesum-min "https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=..." --json -o result.json

Exit codes are unchanged: 0 success, 1 runtime failure (the object has "isSuccess": false), 2 invalid arguments (no JSON is produced).

docs.title: Shape
docs.text:
{
  "isSuccess": true,
  "content": "Summary text",
  "providerId": "ollama",
  "errorMessage": null,
  "modelName": "llama3.2",
  "usage": {
    "promptTokens": 120,
    "completionTokens": 80,
    "totalTokens": 200
  },
  "durationMs": 842.5
}
Field Type Notes isSuccess boolean false for expected failures (network, no subtitles, model errors). content string Summary text; an empty string on failure. providerId string | null Provider that produced the result; null if the pipeline failed before invoking one. errorMessage string | null Failure reason; null on success. modelName string | null Model reported by the provider; null when unknown (for example transcript-only). usage object | null Token counts when the backend reports them; null otherwise. durationMs number | null Time spent in the provider call, in milliseconds (may be fractional); null on failure.

All fields are always present; missing data is null.

docs.title: Failure example
docs.text:
{
  "isSuccess": false,
  "content": "",
  "providerId": "ollama",
  "errorMessage": "model 'llama3.2' not pulled",
  "modelName": "llama3.2",
  "usage": null,
  "durationMs": null
}

docs.title: Notes
docs.text:
• The schema is additive within 0.x: new optional fields may appear, existing fields keep their names and types.
  • --json implies quiet progress on stdout, but progress lines still appear on stderr unless the caller discards stderr.
  • With -o, the file contains JSON; the confirmation message is written to stderr.
  • The same data is available programmatically through SummaryResult in Beesum.Core (see embedding.md).

docs.title: Batch
docs.text:
--batch <file> produces an array by default and JSON Lines with --jsonl. Each object has one extra field, url, at the front:

[
  {
    "url": "https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=abc",
    "isSuccess": true,
    "content": "Summary text",
    "providerId": "ollama",
    "errorMessage": null,
    "modelName": "llama3.2",
    "usage": { "promptTokens": 120, "completionTokens": 80, "totalTokens": 200 },
    "durationMs": 842.5
  }
]

--jsonl writes one compact object per line instead of an array:

{"url":"https://...","isSuccess":true,"content":"...","providerId":"ollama","errorMessage":null,"modelName":"llama3.2","usage":null,"durationMs":12.4}

Batch mode does not add a url field to single-URL output; the schema above is for batch only.

docs.title: Subtitle languages
docs.text:
beesum-min asks yt-dlp for subtitles in the languages you name:

beesum-min "..." --sub-langs en
beesum-min "..." --sub-langs ru,en
beesum-min "..." --sub-langs ru --proxy socks5://127.0.0.1:1080

The default is en. Manual subtitles are preferred by yt-dlp; auto-generated captions are accepted when there is nothing better.

docs.title: Selection
docs.text:
When yt-dlp writes several .vtt files, the first language in your list wins:

  1. ru,en → abc.ru.vtt, fallback to abc.en.vtt;
  2. en,ru → abc.en.vtt, fallback to abc.ru.vtt;
  3. en.* → a file whose tag is en or starts with en- (for example en-US).

If none of the requested languages is present, the first downloaded file is used. That fallback is deliberate: a transcript in the wrong language is still better than a failed run, and the JSON/Language field tells you what you got.

docs.title: Why not en.* by default
docs.text: YouTube exposes dozens of auto-translated variants (en-ar, en-de, ...). en.* matches all of them, turns one subtitle request into a burst, and gets rate limited with HTTP 429. Concrete codes (en, ru, de) are cheaper and more predictable.

docs.title: Translation
docs.text: This is subtitle selection, not translation. --sub-langs ru downloads Russian subtitles if the video has them; it does not translate an English transcript. Prompt-based translation is a separate feature.

docs.title: Library
docs.text:
services.AddBeesum(options =>
{
    options.SubtitleLanguages.Clear();
    options.SubtitleLanguages.Add("ru");
    options.SubtitleLanguages.Add("en");
});

docs.title: MCP server
docs.text: beesum-mcp is a small Model Context Protocol server over stdio. It exposes the same pipeline as the CLI as two tools, so an agent can summarize a YouTube video or a transcript it already has.

docs.title: Install and configure
docs.text:
dotnet tool install -g beesum-mcp

Claude Desktop / Cursor / any MCP client:

{
  "mcpServers": {
    "beesum-min": {
      "command": "beesum-mcp",
      "env": {
        "BEESUM_PROVIDER": "transcript-only",
        "BEESUM_PROXY": "socks5://127.0.0.1:1080"
      }
    }
  }
}

Remove BEESUM_PROXY unless you need one. BEESUM_PROVIDER defaults to transcript-only.

docs.title: summarize_url
docs.text: Argument Type Meaning url string, required YouTube URL. style historian | programmer | neutral Built-in prompt shortcut. format markdown | plaintext | mindmap Output format. instructions string Extra instructions appended to the prompt. timestamps boolean Prefix cues with [hh:mm:ss] and ask the model to keep them. prompt string Full system prompt; replaces style/format. provider string Provider id, overrides BEESUM_PROVIDER.

docs.title: summarize_transcript
docs.text:
Argument Type Meaning text string, required Plain text or WebVTT. input_format text | vtt Default text. style, format, instructions, prompt, provider, timestamps Same as above.

Tool results are a single text content block with the summary. Expected failures (isError: true) carry the pipeline's error message, so the agent does not need to parse stderr.

docs.title: Environment
docs.text:
Variable Default Purpose BEESUM_PROVIDER transcript-only Default provider id. BEESUM_OLLAMA_URL http://localhost:11434 Ollama base URL. BEESUM_OLLAMA_MODEL llama3.2 Ollama model. BEESUM_PROXY unset Passed to yt-dlp as --proxy. BEESUM_SUB_LANGS en Comma-separated subtitle languages. OPENAI_API_KEY unset Enables the OpenAI-compatible provider. BEESUM_OPENAI_URL / BEESUM_OPENAI_MODEL OpenAI / gpt-4o-mini Override endpoint. ANTHROPIC_API_KEY unset Enables Anthropic. GEMINI_API_KEY / GOOGLE_API_KEY unset Enables Gemini.

API keys are read from the server environment only; they never appear in tool arguments or protocol messages.

docs.title: Protocol
docs.text:
• newline-delimited JSON-RPC 2.0 on stdio;
  • initialize, ping, shutdown, tools/list, tools/call;
  • supported protocol versions: 2024-11-05, 2025-03-26, 2025-06-18;
  • stdout carries protocol messages only; logs go to stderr;
  • no resources, prompts, sampling, or HTTP transport.

The server is meant for a local MCP client: one process, one user, one session.

docs.title: Try it by hand
docs.text:
printf '%s\n' \
  '{"jsonrpc":"2.0","id":1,"method":"initialize","params":{"protocolVersion":"2025-06-18","capabilities":{},"clientInfo":{"name":"shell","version":"1"}}}' \
  '{"jsonrpc":"2.0","id":2,"method":"tools/list"}' \
  '{"jsonrpc":"2.0","id":3,"method":"tools/call","params":{"name":"summarize_transcript","arguments":{"text":"Hello world"}}}' \
  | beesum-mcp

docs.title: Packages
docs.text:
Four packages are produced by scripts/pack.sh:

Package Kind Contents Beesum.Core library parser, pipeline, providers, storage Beesum.Testing library in-memory test doubles beesum-min .NET tool the CLI beesum-mcp .NET tool the MCP stdio server

SHA256SUMS is written next to them. Symbol packages (.snupkg) are produced too.

docs.title: Build packages locally
docs.text: bash scripts/pack.sh

docs.title: Install
docs.text:
From nuget.org:

dotnet tool install -g beesum-min
dotnet tool install -g beesum-mcp
dotnet add package Beesum.Core
dotnet add package Beesum.Testing   # in test projects

docs.title: nuget.org: Trusted Publishing
docs.text:
No long-lived NUGET_API_KEY is stored. The NuGet workflow uses GitHub OIDC via NuGet/login@v1; the token lives for one job.

One-time setup:

  1. nuget.org → Account → Trusted Publishing → Add policy
  2. Repository owner: air-catfish
  3. Repository: beesum-min
  4. Workflow file: nuget.yml (the filename, not the workflow display name)
  5. Environment: release
  6. GitHub → Settings → Environments → New environment → release
  7. Add an environment secret: NUGET_USER = your nuget.org profile name, not your email.
  8. Optional: required reviewers as a publish gate.
  9. Push a v* tag, or run Actions → NuGet → Run workflow with an existing tag (for example v0.2.3).

The policy is permanent for a public repository after the first successful publish; private repositories have a seven-day temporary window.

docs.title: GitHub Packages
docs.text:
The release workflow publishes the same packages to GitHub Packages with GITHUB_TOKEN. That source requires authentication for consumers, even when the packages are public:

dotnet nuget add source "https://nuget.pkg.github.com/air-catfish/index.json" `
  --name github --username air-catfish --password "<PAT with read:packages>"

Then install with --add-source github, or put it in nuget.config.

docs.title: Release checklist
docs.text:
1. Set the version in Directory.Build.props (currently 0.2.3).
  2. Create the trusted publishing policy and the release environment secret NUGET_USER (once).
  3. Create a signed tag and push it:
git tag -s v0.2.3 -m "beesum-min 0.2.1"
git verify-tag v0.2.3
git push origin v0.2.3

If you do not have a signing key, create an unsigned tag and enable immutable releases in the repository settings; it is weaker.

  1. The tag runs two workflows: Release (GitHub Packages, Docker image, GitHub release with packages and SHA256SUMS) and NuGet (nuget.org with symbols). For an already existing tag, dispatch NuGet manually.

docs.title: Prompts
docs.text: The three built-in styles (historian, programmer, neutral) are shortcuts, not the product. Anything real goes through a prompt file or extra instructions.

docs.title: Two knobs
docs.text:
--instructions "<text>" appends to the built-in style/format prompt:

beesum-min "..." --instructions "Five bullets for a team lead, no fluff."

--prompt-file <path> replaces the whole system prompt:

beesum-min "..." --prompt-file examples/prompts/tech-lead.md

When a prompt file is set, --style and --format no longer shape the prompt. The transcript is still sent separately as the user message, so never paste the transcript into the prompt file.

From code, the same two fields live on SummaryRequest:

new SummaryRequest(
    transcript,
    PromptStyle.Neutral,
    OutputFormat.Markdown,
    Instructions: "Five bullets.",
    SystemPrompt: null);

docs.title: Output formats
docs.text:
--format selects the prompt shape:

  • markdown — headings and bullets;
  • plaintext — no markup;
  • mindmap — the model returns a nested bullet list; beesum-min wraps it in a valid Mermaid mindmap.

mindmap needs an LLM provider; transcript-only always prints the transcript. Add --timestamps to prefix cues with [hh:mm:ss] and ask the model to keep those times when it cites a moment.

docs.title: Examples
docs.text:
• examples/prompts/tech-lead.md — five bullets, decisions and numbers.
  • examples/prompts/eli5.md — plain-language explanation.
  • examples/prompts/meeting-notes.md — decisions, actions, open questions.

Write prompts that say what to leave out. "Summarize" is not an instruction; "five bullets, no preamble, keep numbers" is.

docs.title: Chunking
docs.text: With chunking enabled, a full SystemPrompt is used for every chunk and for the final combination. A prompt that only makes sense for a finished summary will produce strange partial summaries. Instructions are applied to the final combination; the map phase uses a fixed part-summary instruction.

docs.title: Safety
docs.text:
• Do not put API keys, cookies, or personal data in prompt files.
  • Do not ask the model to output secrets it saw in the transcript; it will.
  • A prompt can change tone and structure, not facts. If the transcript does not contain a number, the model must not invent one.

docs.title: Security
docs.text: The canonical policy is SECURITY.md in the repository.

docs.title: Short version
docs.text:
• Local CLI; MCP is local stdio. Do not expose either to an untrusted network.
  • transcript-only never sends the transcript anywhere. Ollama stays local.
  • API keys come from env variables or the local secret store.
  • Windows uses DPAPI; Unix uses a 0600 file, not encryption yet.
  • yt-dlp runs as a child process with an argument list, not through a shell.
  • MCP summarize_url accepts YouTube hosts only.
  • Docker runs as UID/GID 10001; yt-dlp and deno are pinned and checksummed.
  • No telemetry, no background network activity.

docs.title: Known limitations
docs.text:
• Unix secrets are permission-protected, not encrypted.
  • NuGet packages are not signed; there is no SBOM yet.
  • No rate limit for a local caller.
  • Prompt-injected transcripts can make a summary misleading; no code execution.
  • The git tag is not signed.

docs.title: Report
docs.text: Use GitHub Security Advisories, or the Codeberg issue tracker if GitHub is not available. Do not open a public issue for an unfixed vulnerability.

docs.title: How this is tested
docs.text: No coverage badges, no “100% tested” claims. The suite is small and opinionated.

docs.title: What exists
docs.text:
• 265 tests: Core 192, CLI 53, Testing 8, MCP 12.
  • Provider contract tests: every ILlmProvider must return a stable id, a non-null availability, throw on a null request, and produce consistent metadata.
  • Golden tests: exact prompt strings for all style/format combinations and an exact JSON shape for --json.
  • Deterministic fuzz: 500 pseudo-random strings into the VTT parser, plus monotonic timestamps and CRLF/LF equivalence.
  • MCP protocol tests: initialize, tools/list, tools/call, unknown methods, malformed JSON, VTT input.
  • Real boundary tests: cancellation, timeouts, missing yt-dlp, failed chunks, language preference, path traversal in cache keys.

The suite never touches the network. yt-dlp, HTTP, and Ollama are replaced with in-memory doubles from Beesum.Testing.

docs.title: How it runs
docs.text:
dotnet build beesum-min.slnx -c Release
dotnet run --project tests\Beesum.Core.Tests
dotnet run --project tests\Beesum.Min.Cli.Tests
dotnet run --project tests\Beesum.Testing.Tests
dotnet run --project tests\Beesum.Mcp.Tests

CI runs the same commands on windows-latest and ubuntu-latest, with warnings as errors.

docs.title: What is not tested
docs.text:
• Live YouTube downloads and the proxy path: verified manually on a real video (3blue1brown, fNk_zzaMoSs) through a SOCKS5 proxy.
  • Live API calls: the provider tests use fake HTTP; real keys are not part of CI.
  • Mutation testing: Stryker.NET is not wired in yet, so there is no mutation score.
  • GUI: it lives in a separate private repository.

docs.title: Why no mocking library
docs.text: The doubles are plain classes: InMemoryProcessRunner, InMemoryHttpMessageHandler, InMemoryLlmProvider, and friends. They record calls and queue responses, which keeps tests readable and the package free of a mocking dependency.

docs.title: Versioning
docs.text: The project follows Semantic Versioning 2.0.0.

docs.title: Before 1.0
docs.text:
0.x is explicitly unstable: a minor bump (0.1 → 0.2) may contain breaking changes to the public API. Patch releases (0.1.1) are bug fixes only.

Pin an exact version if you build on Beesum.Core before 1.0:

<PackageReference Include="Beesum.Core" Version="[0.2.0]" />

docs.title: After 1.0
docs.text:
• Breaking changes only in a major version.
  • A public API is deprecated for at least one minor release before removal.
  • Deprecations use [Obsolete] with a migration hint.

docs.title: Packages
docs.text:
Beesum.Core, Beesum.Testing, and the beesum-min tool are versioned together. A tool release may lag a library release only if the CLI did not change.

Pre-release versions use a suffix (0.2.0-rc.1) and are not picked up by default by NuGet ranges.

docs.title: Support
docs.text: Only the latest minor of the current major gets security fixes. There are no maintained LTS branches before 1.0.

docs.title: Release cadence
docs.text: No fixed schedule. Patches when needed, minors when a feature set is coherent and tested. Release notes live in docs/release-notes/.

docs.title: Chat bots and web clients (future)
docs.text: The local CLI stays local. Bots and web clients should talk to a server API, not run yt-dlp on the bot host.

docs.title: Flow
docs.text:
User sends URL
      │
      ▼
Connector verifies webhook / auth
      │
      ▼
POST /v1/jobs  ──► 202 jobId
      │
      ▼
Connector sends "processing"
      │
      ▼
Poll GET /v1/jobs/{id} or receive webhook
      │
      ▼
Send summary + transcript links

docs.title: Connectors
docs.text:
• Telegram: verify the secret token, map chat/user to tenant.
  • Discord: verify interaction signature, defer the response.
  • Slack: verify signing secret, use response_url.
  • Web: normal session/OIDC auth.

Connectors are adapters. They must not own authz, quotas, sandboxing, or storage policy.

docs.title: Formatting
docs.text: Chat platforms have message limits. Send a short summary plus a link to the full Markdown artifact; do not paste a 10k-character transcript into a message.

docs.title: Failure modes
docs.text:
• yt-dlp failure: show a retryable error, not a stack trace.
  • LLM failure: keep the transcript artifact and let the user retry the summary.
  • Timeout: keep the job alive in the queue; the connector should not block.

docs.title: v0.2.0
docs.text: First public release of beesum-min: a transcript-first YouTube summarizer library and CLI, MIT-licensed.

docs.title: Packages
docs.text: Package Version What it is Beesum.Core 0.2.0 Models, contracts, WebVTT parser, yt-dlp service, LLM providers, pipeline, storage Beesum.Testing 0.2.0 In-memory doubles and AddBeesumTesting() for hermetic tests beesum-min (tool) 0.2.0 The command-line host beesum-mcp (tool) 0.2.0 MCP stdio server for agents

docs.title: Highlights
docs.text:
• Public, documented Core API. AddBeesum(Action<BeesumOptions>) + IOptions<BeesumOptions>, optional ILogger<T> integration, and ISummarizerPipelineFactory for run-time provider selection. Implementations are internal; interfaces, models, and DI are the contract.
  • Summary metadata. SummaryResult reports ProviderId, ModelName, Usage (token counts), and Duration.
  • JSON output. beesum-min --json emits one stable object for scripts; see docs/json-output.md.
  • Trusted Publishing. nuget.org publishes through GitHub OIDC; no long-lived NuGet API key is stored.
  • Clips and saves. --from/--to, --save-vtt, and --save-transcript turn a long video into a local note.
  • Timecodes and mindmaps. --timestamps keeps [hh:mm:ss]; --format mindmap returns Mermaid.
  • MCP. beesum-mcp exposes the pipeline as two tools for Claude/Cursor/other MCP clients.
  • Chunking. Long transcripts are split and reduced with map-reduce; usage and duration are summed across calls (--chunk-tokens, --no-chunk).
  • Beesum.Testing. InMemory* stores, yt-dlp/parser/process/HTTP doubles, so consumers can test without disk, network, yt-dlp, or Ollama.
  • Transcript-first privacy. The default transcript-only provider never sends the transcript anywhere; ollama talks only to the local instance.

docs.title: Install
docs.text:
dotnet tool install -g beesum-min
dotnet add package Beesum.Core

docs.title: Verification
docs.text:
• dotnet build beesum-min.slnx -c Release — 0 warnings, 0 errors.
  • Tests — 122 green: Beesum.Core.Tests 103, Beesum.Min.Cli.Tests 11, Beesum.Testing.Tests 8.
  • Offline smoke: beesum-min --local-vtt samples/demo/smoke.vtt and beesum-min --local-vtt samples/demo/smoke.vtt --json.
  • Packages verified with dotnet pack (nupkg + snupkg, icon, README, XML docs).
  • Tool verified from a local feed: dotnet tool install --tool-path artifacts/tool beesum-min --add-source artifacts/packages --version 0.2.0; --help, JSON success, and JSON failure (exit code 1) checked.
  • Self-contained win-x64 publish verified end to end (77.9 MB, JSON output).

docs.title: Known limitations
docs.text:
• The API follows 0.x: names and shapes may change before 1.0.
  • No chunking of long transcripts; very long videos may exceed the model context.
  • The CLI exposes Ollama and transcript-only; the OpenAI-compatible provider is library-only for now.
  • ITranscriptCache and ISummaryHistory are contracts, not yet wired into the pipeline.
  • Docker images are built and published by CI; the local machine used for this release has no Docker daemon.
  • dotnet test is unreliable on some locked-down Windows machines; run the test projects with dotnet run there (see the troubleshooting page).

docs.title: Server architecture (future)
docs.text:
This page describes the planned service layer. It is not implemented in the beesum-min repository.

CLI / MCP / Telegram / Discord / Web
                │
          HTTPS + webhooks
                ▼
        Beesum.Server (ASP.NET)
  auth, tenants, quotas, validation,
  jobs, artifacts, audit
                │
                ▼
        Beesum.Worker (container)
  yt-dlp sandbox + Beesum.Core + LLM
                │
                ▼
        Postgres / Redis / S3

docs.title: Repository split
docs.text:
• beesum-min — local CLI, Core package, MCP; no server dependencies.
  • beesum-server — ASP.NET API, worker, connectors; references Beesum.Core as a NuGet package.
  • Beesum.Connectors.* — Telegram/Discord/Slack adapters; call the HTTP API, never yt-dlp directly.

docs.title: API shape
docs.text:
POST /v1/jobs          -> 202 { jobId }
GET  /v1/jobs/{id}     -> status, result, usage
GET  /v1/jobs/{id}/artifacts/{kind}

Long work is queued; the API process never downloads subtitles itself.

docs.title: Why not reuse the CLI process
docs.text: Running a CLI process per request is possible for a prototype, but it lacks tenant isolation, quotas, retries, and structured cancellation. The worker should call Beesum.Core directly.

docs.title: Server security model
docs.text: For a multi-tenant deployment, every item below is mandatory.

docs.title: Identity and tenancy
docs.text:
• OIDC for people, scoped API keys for bots.
  • tenant_id on every row, cache key, object path, and queue message.
  • RBAC checks on every job/artifact read.
  • Row-level security or a single tenant-aware repository layer.

docs.title: Worker isolation
docs.text:
• Separate worker service; no public ingress.
  • Non-root container, read-only rootfs, seccomp, no host mounts.
  • Egress allowlist; reject file://, localhost, link-local and private IPs.
  • Per-job temp directory, cleaned up in finally.
  • CPU/RAM/time limits; kill the whole process tree.
  • No user-provided yt-dlp arguments, cookies, or paths.

docs.title: Queues and quotas
docs.text:
• Idempotency key per request.
  • Per-tenant concurrency and daily quotas.
  • Retry with backoff, dead-letter queue, cancellation.
  • Input and token limits before calling an LLM.

docs.title: Secrets and storage
docs.text:
• KMS/envelope encryption for per-tenant keys and cookies.
  • Tenant-prefixed object storage; signed, short-lived download URLs.
  • No transcripts or keys in logs.
  • Retention, deletion, and export policies.

docs.title: API and output
docs.text:
• Request validation, payload limits, CORS/CSRF, security headers.
  • Markdown/HTML sanitization and CSP.
  • Model output is untrusted; do not execute instructions found in a transcript.

docs.title: Operations
docs.text:
• Audit log, metrics without transcript content, traces, alerts.
  • Backups and tested restore.
  • Signed images/SBOM, dependency scanning, isolated network.
  • Authz, SSRF, path traversal, resource-exhaustion, and prompt-injection tests.

docs.title: Tenancy
docs.text: The current local storage (FileTranscriptCache, JsonSummaryHistory, FileSettingsStore) is designed for one user. A server needs tenant-aware replacements.

docs.title: Minimum model
docs.text:
Tenant 1─* User
Tenant 1─* Job 1─* Artifact
Tenant 1─* ApiKey
Tenant 1─* AuditEvent

docs.title: Rules
docs.text:
• Every query includes tenant_id; no unscoped Find(id).
  • Object keys: tenants/{tenantId}/jobs/{jobId}/{kind}.
  • Cache keys include tenant and source; a global transcript cache is a leak.
  • Quotas are per tenant, not per process.
  • Deletion removes database rows, objects, caches, and queue messages.
  • An admin UI must not bypass tenant filters by accident.

docs.title: Testing
docs.text: Write an integration test where tenant A requests tenant B's job/artifact and expects 404 (not 403, to avoid existence leaks). Run it for every endpoint.

docs.title: dotnet test aborts with Win32Exception (5) on Windows 11 build 28000
docs.text: Status: environment issue, not a Beesum bug. This page is a ready-to-paste report for microsoft/vstest.

docs.title: Summary
docs.text:
dotnet test aborts before any test runs, on every .NET project, with:

Unhandled exception. System.ComponentModel.Win32Exception (5): Access is denied.
   at System.Diagnostics.Process.GetProcessHandle(Int32 access, Boolean throwIfExited)
   at System.Diagnostics.Process.GetOrOpenProcessHandle()
   at System.Diagnostics.Process.EnsureWatchingForExit()
   at System.Diagnostics.Process.set_EnableRaisingEvents(Boolean value)
   at Microsoft.VisualStudio.TestPlatform.PlatformAbstractions.ProcessHelper.SetExitCallback(...)
   at Microsoft.VisualStudio.TestPlatform.TestHost.DefaultEngineInvoker.SetParentProcessExitCallback(...)

Reproduced with a stock dotnet new xunit project, so it is not specific to any repository.

docs.title: Root cause observed
docs.text:
A DOTNET_STARTUP_HOOKS probe that logs the integrity SID of the process token (GetTokenInformation(TokenIntegrityLevel) + ConvertSidToStringSid) reports:

Process Integrity dotnet (MSBuild) S-1-16-8192 (Medium) vstest.console (hosted by dotnet) S-1-16-8192 (Medium) testhost S-1-16-4096 (Low)

From inside testhost:

OpenProcess(SYNCHRONIZE, parentPid)          -> OK
OpenProcess(PROCESS_ALL_ACCESS, parentPid)   -> ERROR_ACCESS_DENIED (5)

DefaultEngineInvoker.SetParentProcessExitCallback calls Process.EnableRaisingEvents, and .NET opens the parent process with PROCESS_ALL_ACCESS. A Low-integrity process cannot obtain write access to a Medium-integrity process, so the call throws and the exception is not caught: testhost dies before test discovery, and the run ends with TESTRUNABORT.

The low integrity is applied to testhost by the platform, not by the project: the same happens under a Task Scheduler task and a WMI-spawned process (i.e. outside any harness sandbox), and testhost.exe is a valid Microsoft-signed binary (asInvoker manifest).

docs.title: Minimal repro
docs.text:
mkdir C:\temp\repro
cd C:\temp\repro
dotnet new xunit
dotnet test

docs.title: Expected
docs.text: Tests are discovered and executed.

docs.title: Actual
docs.text:
error TESTRUNABORT: Test run aborted.
Unhandled exception. System.ComponentModel.Win32Exception (5): Access is denied.

docs.title: Environment
docs.text:
• Windows 11 Pro, version 10.0.28000 (build 28000)
  • .NET SDK 10.0.403, runtime 10.0.14
  • VSTest 18.7.0-release-26523-112
  • Microsoft.NET.Test.Sdk 17.14.1 and 18.11.0 (both fail)
  • xunit 2.9.3 and xunit.v3 3.2.2 (both fail under dotnet test)

docs.title: Workarounds
docs.text:
• xunit v3 / Microsoft.Testing.Platform: run the test project as an executable: dotnet run --project tests\Beesum.Core.Tests. This bypasses testhost and works even while the machine is in this state.
  • xunit v2 / VSTest: no supported workaround; tests have to be executed in-process by a custom runner.
